ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

Role Summary

As a Research Engineer on the software side, you will design and harden the codebase, tools and distributed services that let our scientists train and ship frontier-scale models. You do not need prior ML experience; what matters is writing clean, reliable code that scales.

You will join our Research Software Engineering team to build and maintain shared dev-tools, evaluation & data pipelines, training framework, cluster tooling and CI/CD.

Location: Paris / Warsaw / Zurich / London (hybrid) or remote EU/UK with one hub visit per month.

What will you do

• Accelerate researchers by owning the complex parts of large-scale pipelines and delivering robust internal tooling.

• Interface research with product: expose clean APIs, automate model pushes, surface live metrics.

• Write efficient, well-tested Python and systems code; enforce code review, CI, and observability.

• Design and optimise distributed services (Kubernetes / SLURM, thousands-of-GPU jobs).

• Prototype utilities (CLI, dashboards) and carry them through to stable, shared libraries.

About the Research Engineering team

Based in Paris and London, our REs move fluidly along the research ↔ production spectrum. Engineers can rotate between Platform and Embedded tracks as their interests evolve.

About you

• Master’s in Computer Science (or equivalent experience).

• 4 + years building and operating large-scale or distributed systems.

• Strong software-design instincts: modular code, tests, CI/CD, observability.

• Fluency in Python plus one systems language (C++, Rust, Go or Java).

• Hands-on with container orchestration and schedulers (Kubernetes / K8s, SLURM, or similar).

• Comfortable profiling performance, optimising I/O, and automating workflows.

• Self-starter, low-ego, collaborative, high-energy.

Nice-to-haves

• Exposure to ML workloads or data-processing pipelines.

• Experience with GPU clusters or CUDA.

• Open-source contributions or widely used internal tools.

Location and Remote

This role is primarily based at one of our European offices (Paris, Warsaw, Zurich and London). We will prioritize candidates who either reside there or are open to relocating. We strongly believe in the value of in-person collaboration to foster strong relationships and seamless communication within our team. In certain specific situations, we will also consider remote candidates based in one of the countries listed in this job posting — currently France & UK. In that case, we ask all new hires to visit our local office:

• for the first week of their onboarding (accommodation and travelling covered)

• then at least 3 days per month

WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link.

PRIVACY POLICY

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

jobs.description: Amazon Lightsail makes AWS accessible to developers and business customers who want to get their cloud stacks running in seconds without the complexity of traditional infrastructure. As a Software Development Engineer II on the Lightsail team, you will build features and services that simplify compute, storage, networking, and website hosting for customers who need things to just work. The team is expanding quickly, adding new capabilities like website hosting and agent hosting, and you will help shape what comes next. You will work across the full software development lifecycle, from understanding customer problems through design, implementation, testing, deployment, and operations. If you are an engineer who enjoys building products you would actually use yourself, and you want to do that at AWS scale, we would like to talk to you. Key job responsibilities - Design and build features for Amazon Lightsail's distributed systems, working in Java, Go, JavaScript, and React across both backend services and frontend experiences. - Collaborate with partner teams across AWS — including Amazon EC2, Amazon Route 53, Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) — to integrate Lightsail capabilities with the broader AWS ecosystem. - Own the operational health of the services you build by identifying root causes of production issues and driving permanent fixes, ensuring customers experience reliable performance. - Participate actively in design reviews and code reviews, providing constructive feedback to teammates and mentoring other engineers on writing clean, maintainable code. - Evaluate new technologies and approaches, including generative artificial intelligence tools, to improve team productivity and the quality of solutions delivered to customers. A day in the life You start your morning checking operational dashboards for a Lightsail service you recently launched, then join a design review where you and a teammate work through how to integrate a new hosting capability with an existing AWS service. After lunch, you pick up a feature task, writing backend logic in Java and wiring up the React console so customers can try it out. Later, you review a pull request from a teammate, leave detailed feedback, and update documentation so the next engineer who touches this code can ramp up quickly. About the team Amazon Lightsail sits within AWS and has a distinctive mission: make cloud infrastructure simple and approachable for non-enterprise customers. While we run on the same AWS infrastructure that powers the world's largest workloads, our focus is on removing complexity so developers and small businesses can launch and scale without a steep learning curve. We are an inclusive team that values knowledge sharing and mentorship, and we intentionally assign projects to help each engineer grow. Right now we are investing in new hosting and agent capabilities, so there is plenty of room to have a direct impact on what we build next.

ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD.

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career.

THE ROLE

AMD is seeking a Lead Engineer, Behind-the-Meter Power Infrastructure to act as a client representative and technical validation lead for gas-to-power and behind-the-meter data center power projects.

In this role, you will review and validate end-to-end power solutions from gas supply and pipeline infrastructure through generation, alternators, BESS, substations, medium-voltage distribution, protection systems, and final delivery to the data center load. You will collaborate with developers, EPCs, utilities, gas suppliers, OEMs, consultants, and internal AMD teams to determine whether proposed solutions are technically sound, schedule-realistic, aligned with applicable permitting requirements, and capable of reaching commercial operation.

THE PERSON

The ideal candidate is an experienced power infrastructure technical leader with demonstrated judgment from an owner/client perspective. You understand how gas supply, permitting, generation, electrical collection, substations, controls, and commissioning come together to deliver reliable power to a mission-critical data center.

You can independently evaluate assumptions, constructively identify design and schedule gaps, and translate complex technical risks into clear, evidence-based recommendations for technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Act as AMD’s technical client representative for behind-the-meter power infrastructure projects.
• Validate the full power chain from gas supply, pipeline lateral, easements, gas quality, fuel conditioning, and gas distribution through generation and electrical delivery.
• Review reciprocating engine, turbine, alternator, BESS, switchgear, transformer, substation, and protection-system designs.
• Assess whether proposed power solutions can meet data center load, redundancy, power-quality, maintainability, reliability, and commercial operation requirements.
• Review single-line diagrams, gas-flow diagrams, basis-of-design documents, permit matrices, equipment specifications, commissioning plans, and project schedules.
• Validate gas supply assumptions, pipeline routes, right-of-way and easement status, crossing permits, gas pressure, gas quality, and backup fuel strategies.
• Evaluate generator sizing, derating, heat rate, emissions controls, alternator performance, paralleling switchgear, and maintenance strategies.
• Review medium-voltage and high-voltage architecture, including MV collectors, main power transformers, substations, ring bus design, relay protection, grounding, and islanding logic.
• Support review of grid-forming BESS, load-step response, dynamic stability, frequency control, harmonic performance, and AI workload transient behavior.
• Identify missing permits, unresolved approvals, construction-sequencing risks, equipment lead-time risks, and commissioning gaps.
• Define technical decision points for design freeze, permit clearance, initial gas delivery, initial generator operation, synchronization, load testing, islanding, failover testing, and commercial operation.
• Prepare clear technical risk summaries, executive briefings, open-item trackers, and recommendations regarding project readiness and conditions required to proceed.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

• Experience in power generation, data center power infrastructure, gas-fired generation, utility systems, microgrids, industrial energy projects, or comparable complex power infrastructure.
• Strong understanding of natural gas infrastructure, including pipeline interconnects, laterals, metering stations, gas quality, pressure regulation, fuel conditioning, easements, right-of-way, and crossing permits.
• Experience with reciprocating generators, gas turbines, alternators, paralleling switchgear, emissions-control systems, continuous emissions monitoring systems, and plant commissioning, or comparable generation technologies.
• Knowledge of BESS, grid-forming inverters, islanded power systems, black start, load shedding, and non-export controls.
• Experience reviewing medium-voltage and high-voltage systems, including 13.8 kV, 34.5 kV, 138 kV, 230 kV, 345 kV, or comparable infrastructure.
• Familiarity with substations, main power transformers, switchgear, relays, short-circuit studies, protection coordination, arc-flash studies, grounding, and synchronization.
• Ability to review and interpret load-flow, dynamic stability, electromagnetic transient (EMT), rate-of-change-of-frequency (RoCoF), frequency-nadir, and harmonic studies.
• Working knowledge of applicable permitting and regulatory requirements for areas such as air emissions, stormwater, pipelines, road and rail crossings, fire protection, hazardous materials, LNG, and utility interconnection.
• Experience collaborating with EPCs, developers, utilities, gas suppliers, OEMs, environmental consultants, construction teams, and other relevant project stakeholders.
• Ability to communicate complex technical risks clearly and effectively to engineering and non-engineering stakeholders, including executives, legal, procurement, and finance teams.

ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS

• Bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Power Systems Engineering, Energy Engineering, Civil Engineering, a related technical field, or equivalent relevant experience in complex power or infrastructure projects.
• Professional Engineer license preferred but not required unless necessary for specific job responsibilities.
• Equivalent experience in large-scale power generation, utility, data center, industrial infrastructure, or comparable projects will be considered.

Being good neighbors – helping people, investing in our communities, and making the world a better place – is who we are at State Farm. We're moving with urgency to become a Next Gen Good Neighbor, with technology that strengthens human connections and enhances the customer experience. As an employee, you'll spend less time navigating systems and more time applying judgment, empathy, and expertise in the moments that matter most.

Grow Your Skills, Grow Your Potential

Responsibilities

Join our team as a Property Field Inspection Claim Specialist and showcase your expertise in handling accident and weather-related claims for homeowners, commercial properties, and large losses.

We are looking for an experienced and highly skilled professional to contribute to our dynamic team. State Farm is on the cutting edge with the use of technology to support claim employees in developing enhanced skillsets to support and protect our policyholders. Not Human or Digital. Human + Digital, working together. You will be the first point of contact to meet with our insureds, explain coverage, estimate damages, and help them through the claims process while providing Remarkable service.

Key Responsibilities:

• Conduct on-site inspections and assessments of property damages for both residential and commercial claims
• Collaborate with policyholders, insurance agents, and other involved parties to gather information and resolve claims efficiently
• May occasionally require interacting with parties who express strong emotions or concerns about ongoing inspections or claim resolutions
• Provide exceptional customer service throughout the claims process, addressing inquiries and concerns promptly and professionally
• Gather necessary evidence, document findings, and prepare detailed reports to support the claims handling process
• Investigate and adjust both personal and commercial property claims with exposures up to $500,000
• Evaluate coverage and policy terms to determine the validity of claims and ensure compliance with local regulations
• Negotiate and settle claims within the authorized limits, considering policy provisions, industry standards, and company guidelines

Where you'll work: This position is located in Yuma, AZ. Competitive candidates should reside within one of the listed zip codes and will service this same territory:

85321 85328 85333 85334 85336 85346 85347 85349 85350 85352 85356 85364 85365 85367

This is a Remote-Field position in which you will work from home and utilize a mobile office/vehicle for in-person appointments. Although the primary work location is in the field, with a commutable distance from home, there will be opportunities for virtual work to be completed at home. Additionally, there may be occasions where you will be required to travel outside your assigned area to assist in other territories.

Hours of operation are continually evaluated and may change based on business need. Successful candidates are able and willing to work flexible schedules and may be asked to work overtime and/or irregular hours.

Qualifications

Competitive candidates must demonstrate:

• Ability to investigate problems, evaluate information, and make well-supported decisions
• Ability to interpret detailed policies, guidelines, or technical information and apply them accurately to real-world situations
• Ability to quickly learn unfamiliar concepts, processes, and terminology and apply that knowledge accurately in practical situations
• Ability to effectively interact with policyholders, agents, and other stakeholders to move claims forward efficiently
• Effective communication and interpersonal skills to handle difficult/emotional conversations with a customer-minded focus
• Detail-oriented with strong organizational and analytical skills
• Proficiency in using mobile/desktop tools to document and support claims both in the field and remotely
• Physical agility to allow for: walking; bending, reaching, kneeling, squatting, stooping, frequent lifting, carrying, unfolding, and climbing a ladder; ability to utilizing appropriate equipment in accordance with safety guidelines to traverse roofs at various heights and pitches for inspection of both residential and commercial structures; ability to crawl in tight spaces to gather information needed during the adjustment of a claim.
• May be required to complete Rope and Harness Safety Training
•

A valid driver’s license is required, as driving is an essential function of this job. A Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) will be requested as part of the pre-employment background check.

• Bachelor’s Degree in a related field such as Risk Management, Insurance, Business, Construction Management or a similar discipline
• Customer service experience (e.g., assisting customers, handling inquiries/concerns professionally, communicating clearly and empathetically), demonstrating transferable skills that support client interactions in a Claims environment
• Understanding of property insurance concepts, including coverage fundamentals and general claim handling practices
• Baseline knowledge of residential and commercial building construction and building components/materials
Familiarity with water mitigation principles and inspection processes
• Working knowledge of Xactimate and XactContents

Our Benefits

Because work-life balance is a priority at State Farm, compensation is based on our standard 38:45-hour work week!

jobs.description: Job Details: As a Senior IT Product Owner, you are accountable for maximizing measurable business value and ensuring the right problems are solved before production investment .
